title: Custom error classes and discriminated error unions
hook: The built-in Error class is enough for generic failures, but domain code needs typed errors — HttpError with statusCode, ValidationError with field paths. Subclass Error for instanceof checks, or use discriminated unions when you prefer Result-style data.

blocks.text: A **custom error class** extends the built-in **Error** and adds domain fields — `statusCode`, `field`, `retryable`. Callers catch with `instanceof HttpError` and branch on those fields. An alternative is a **discriminated error union**: `{ kind: 'validation'; fields: string[] } | { kind: 'not-found'; id: string }` returned inside `Result<T, AppError>` without throwing at all. Both patterns give typed failure information; classes work well with throw/catch middleware, unions work well with Result pipelines.

entries.plainDefinition: class HttpError extends Error with extra properties. Preserves stack when thrown correctly.
entries.example: class HttpError extends Error { constructor(public statusCode: number, message: string) { super(message); } }

entries.plainDefinition: A union of plain objects tagged with kind or code — no class, fits Result errors.
entries.example: { kind: 'timeout'; ms: number } | { kind: 'auth'; reason: string }

entries.plainDefinition: ES2022 Error constructor option linking an inner error — like C# InnerException.
String label on Error, often set to the class name for logging and serialization.

blocks.text: An API gateway maps errors to HTTP responses: 404 for not-found, 429 for rate limit, 500 for unexpected. If every failure is `new Error('...')`, you parse message strings — fragile and untestable. Typed errors let middleware do `if (err instanceof NotFoundError) res.status(404)` in one place. In C#, you might throw `LeaseExpiredException`; in TypeScript, subclass Error or return a tagged union. Pick one style per layer and stick to it.

blocks.title: Set prototype for instanceof in transpiled code
blocks.body: When targeting ES5, subclassing Error requires Object.setPrototypeOf(this, HttpError.prototype) in the constructor so instanceof works after transpilation. Modern targets (ES2015+) usually handle this automatically.

items.title: Throwing stack — use Error subclasses
items.body: Express middleware, global handlers, and deep call stacks benefit from throw + instanceof.

items.title: Expected outcomes — use union in Result
items.body: Validation and business rules return { kind: 'validation', fields } inside Result — no stack walk.

items.title: Normalize at the boundary
items.body: Convert unknown catch values and plain union errors to AppError before logging.

items.title: Serialize carefully
items.body: Error properties are non-enumerable — JSON.stringify(err) is often {}. Use a toJSON or mapper for APIs.

diagram.title: Error shapes in a layered app
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  DOMAIN[Domain layer Result or throw AppError]
  DOMAIN --> SERVICE[Service catches unknown normalizes]
  SERVICE --> HTTP[HTTP middleware maps to status]
  HTTP --> LOG[Logger gets name message cause stack]
  subgraph shapes
    CLASS[HttpError extends Error]
    UNION[kind validation not-found]
  end
  DOMAIN --> CLASS
  DOMAIN --> UNION

snippet.label: HttpError subclass with cause
snippet.explanation: Lines 1–9: statusCode on the error for middleware mapping. Line 6: cause chains inner fetch failures like C# InnerException. Lines 11–15: specific subclass for instanceof NotFoundError checks.

snippet.label: Discriminated AppError union for Result
snippet.explanation: Lines 1–4: kind discriminant enables exhaustive switch. Lines 8–14: no throw for expected validation/not-found — errors are data. HTTP layer switches on error.kind for status codes.

snippet.label: Express error middleware mapping
snippet.explanation: Lines 2–4: instanceof HttpError maps to correct HTTP status. Lines 5–8: generic Error logs stack and cause. Lines 9–11: non-Error throws still handled — unknown boundary discipline.

blocks.title: Dozens of empty custom exception classes
blocks.body: class FooException extends Error {} with no extra fields adds no value over Error with a good message. Add fields callers need — statusCode, field, retryable — or use a union.

blocks.title: Mixing throw and Result in the same layer
blocks.body: A function that sometimes throws HttpError and sometimes returns Result confuses callers. Pick throw OR Result per layer; convert at boundaries.

blocks.text: Custom Error subclasses work across async boundaries if you throw the same instance — unlike some serialized RPC errors that become plain objects and fail instanceof. For distributed systems, prefer stable error codes (kind: 'NOT_FOUND') in JSON over class names. Error.cause (ES2022) is the idiomatic inner chain — log err.cause in structured logging. In monorepos, put AppError union in a shared package; HTTP adapters map kind to status. Avoid deep inheritance trees — flat Error + code beats Exception → ApplicationException → DomainException. Production proof: alert on error.name distribution; spike in generic Error means missing classification.

snippet.label: instanceof breaks after JSON round-trip — use codes
snippet.explanation: Lines 1–3: JSON.stringify on Error loses data — instanceof fails across services. Lines 6–14: stable codes survive serialization — pattern for microservices boundaries.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Creating ten exception classes with no extra fields. Not knowing JSON.stringify(Error) is {}. Assuming instanceof works after Redis or HTTP deserialization. Mixing Result and throw in one function without a boundary rule.

interviewTakeaways: Extend Error for throw/catch middleware; use discriminated unions for Result-based domain errors.
Set name and use cause for inner chains — mirrors C# InnerException.
instanceof breaks across serialization — use stable error codes at service boundaries.
60s: HttpError with statusCode for middleware. Union with kind for Result. cause for wrap once. No empty exception classes. JSON.stringify err is empty.
Follow-up: when would you choose union errors over Error subclasses?
commonPitfalls: Empty exception classes with no domain fields — use Error or a union with data.
JSON.stringify(err) expecting custom fields — non-enumerable properties are lost.
Strong answer: 'Subclass for stack+middleware, union for Result, cause once at boundary, wire codes for RPC.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS Error subclassing has prototype pitfalls on ES5 targets. TypeScript adds typing for custom fields on the subclass.
C# LeaseExpiredException is caught by type at compile time. TypeScript HttpError needs instanceof at runtime in catch — no typed catch clause.
